items.q: Did OpenAI win the Clay Millennium Prize?
items.a: The video **opener says yes**. The quoted statement is **finite-time blowup with smooth forcing** / forced blowup in **R3 and T3**. Lean can check that. The **$1M Clay problem** is **unforced** existence and smoothness. Keep them apart.

items.q: What did the sprint cost versus the prize?
items.a: ~**10,000 agents**, ~**88 hours**, **probably north of $10 million** — for a **$1 million** prize. Primeagen: the prize is not the business case.

sections.title: Year of drafts, then a rumor

items.q: What had Buckmaster and Alpöge already done?
items.a: ~A year on a Millennium project using **Claude + Codex / GPT-5.6 Soul / Astra**. An LLM proof around **August 15** ("the most horrendous I have ever read") that **Lean verified around August 22**.

items.q: What actually turned OpenAI's fleet on?
items.a: A **September 3 rumor** that Anthropic had solved an open problem. Primeagen: labs will not search an infinite space speculatively. **Belief it is solvable** unlocked tens of millions of compute.

items.q: What did Buckmaster ask about training?
items.a: Whether the model had been **trained on a year of Codex sessions** for an unusual forced-blowup attack they had not advertised. Answer: the model does not **look up** user data. Training question: **no answer**. Primeagen rejects theft/fraud; treats **deidentified sneak-in** as plausible.

items.q: Why offer the academics all the accolades?
items.a: Bubeck texts: concurrent discoveries, **recognize your priority**, share prompts. Primeagen finds that **suspicious if truly independent**. His budget theory: **cannot let Anthropic win**. Punchline: if the stack works, point **10k agents / 88 hours at P vs NP**.
